Hi Anette, 

Colors and the visuals is a very small part of branding.
Branding for a startup is a lot more than that. It involves tone, story, look and feel, values, identity etc. 

You can read about it in more details here: https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-branding

For example: I would perhaps, if possible, try to make the following optimisations. These are all individual parts of branding:
1. Voice: It sounds too robotic. Humans are emotional beings, and a monotonic, unnatural, robotic voice does not make people take action. Is it possible to have a more natural narration? 
2. Speed: Is it a bit slow? If you think there are some areas where a pause is not necessary, feel free to omit it. 
3. Tone: Currently it sounds a lot professional, as though giving a presentation. Do you want to have the brand tone formal or a bit playful or anything else? There's no right or wrong, it's just what you think fits best with the market. 
4. Values: "AudioCat is bringing you new gaming experience..." This is a good as an introduction but it doesn't motivate or help clarify what problem is getting solved right? For example: "The online gaming industry is broken in terms of accessibility. Only 7% of the video games in the world are accessible. AudioCat solves this problem as it is the world's first ever fully accessible multiplayer audiogame platform"

These are a few very small suggestions, but they are not urgent to be implemented right away. 

The demo is good to go as it is :)

If you have any doubts or would like to brainstorm, please feel free to schedule a meeting at a time which works for you.

Workwize is DE oplossing voor thuiswerken. Via het Workwize platform nemen wij alle uitdagingen van het van thuiswerken weg. Workwize helpt zowel de gezondheid als productiviteit van de medewerkers optimaal te houden in deze nieuwe manier van werken. Door een goede thuiswerkplek kan de scheiding tussen werk en privé gewaarborgd worden en niet onbelangrijk; blijft de werknemer zich thuis ook verbonden voelen met het bedrijf.

Hoe gaat dit precies in zijn werk? Workwize is een platform waarop de werknemer, in een eigen ‘tailor-made’ software omgeving, producten/diensten m.b.t. thuis werken kan bestellen. Hiermee bied jij als werkgever de mogelijkheid een complete kantoorervaring thuis te realiseren (bijvoorbeeld stoel, bureau, noise cancelling headphones, monitor, koffie, maar eventueel ook een borrelpakket voor een digitale bedrijfsborrel). De werkgever bepaalt wat voor producten en diensten werknemers kunnen afnemen en welk budget beschikbaar is. Kortom jij behoudt volledige controle en wij voeren uit.  

Je kunt heel laagdrempelig instappen want ons platform is geheel op basis van ‘no-use-no-pay’ Zowel huren/leasen als kopen is mogelijk en daarnaast is elk abonnement maandelijks op te zeggen! Neem dus gerust een kijkje op goworkwize.com.

Al onze producten kennen voordelige inkoopprijzen door partnerships met o.a. DELL, INTERSTUHL en STAPLES. Ook houden we met het samenstellen van ons assortiment rekening met duurzaamheid.

Op dit moment hebben we al ruim 2000 accounts live en succesvolle samenwerkingen met o.a. Jacobs Douwe Egberts, Otrium, en Hikma!

With Unless, you could create personalized journeys based on interest. For example, if your Facebook audience is interested in "Tesla" and "DIY", personalize your website to highlight the electric kits and the DIY aspect of Infento rides. 
If your FB target is "parents age 20-25" you can safely ditch the kit targeted at 6-14 year-olds and highlight the "Explorer" instead. 

3) "We are focusing strongly on retargeting people on Facebook." 
Unless can track which pages someone visited and for how long, so you could, for example, set up different retargeting campaigns based on the products people showed the most interest in. 
For example, if someone viewed the "Genius Kit" for 10 minutes, add them to the "interested in Genius Kit" audience. Next, use this information to create a retargeting audience on Facebook and a personalized version of your website that is all about the "Genius Kit".  

4) "Hotjar indicates that people tend to get confused by the different Kits they can choose from."
You could use a self-segmentation widget and ask people how old their child is. Then, use personalization to change the order of the kits according to what would be most suitable for someone's kid. You could also leave out certain kits. For example, someone with a 10-year-old child doesn't need to see the "Explorer Kit". Self-segmentation is really powerful as people tend to share a lot of information if they believe it will result in a better UX and targeted product recommendation.

Hey Mayank,

I came across your post regarding conversions on www.engineerbabu.com.
Firstly I must say, it's a pretty good website and moreover you've done a fantastic work in making it so much successful! Kudos to that!

Now i am no expert to advise you on how to make the website better for conversions, you and some few know it better; but i can surely share what worked for me to have a 'wow' factor, for my website www.pratikrenuse.com (99% people whom i shared my website with gave an amazing feedback, helped me get dozens of interviews in top companies etc) 

Here are a few things:
1. Numbers: Numbers give people a sense of trust, they can quantify and measure (in psychological terms, it gives them a power to decide). You might want to display numbers on the home page (rather than in the second pages) to create an initial impact on the users mind.

2. User flow: When i see the website's first page, putting myself in the shoes of a senior executive or a manager who has to decide on, whom to outsource the project; there are too many options to choose from on the home page: get a free quote, how it works, down there's also a section which takes the potential customer outside to entrepreneur's website! perhaps this can be simplified (there are tools like hotjar which tell about the User's behaviour on the website). "Less is better - Google" ;) 

3. Tagline: The tagline is the first thing a user sees when he comes to the website, in a single sentence he wants to know about the company and how the company can be beneficial to him. The "let's chat" is a nice initiator but if it's the first thing the user sees, it might come as a bit pushy and not help develop trust at the back of his mind. Upon that, the chat box which appears as soon as the site loads might be another distractor!

These were just a few things from my side, i hope they might be useful! Let me know if i can be of any other help to you!

All the best

One characteristic of digital marketing is that you have to try and see what happens and make some adjustments. Example :  Increase by x% web visit... and on which target, because if you increase visits of people not interested by your website, it is not very useful ;-) 

When it's done, you need to set some SMART objectives on each channel you choose (twitter, facebook, linkedIn, snapchat, etc ...)   ...
